title: Orders Dakota Access Pipeline to Proceed
description_short: Trump signed a memorandum directing agencies to expedite review and approval of the Dakota Access Pipeline after its prior delay.
description_medium: On January 24, 2017, Trump directed federal agencies to expedite review of approvals for the Dakota Access Pipeline after a prior delay. The memorandum instructed the Army and Army Corps of Engineers to review permits and easements, and to consider whether to change earlier decisions and environmental reviews. It also acknowledged that approvals remained subject to applicable law.
description_long: Trump’s January 24, 2017 memorandum instructed the Army and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to review and, where warranted and permitted by law, expedite approvals needed to construct and operate the Dakota Access Pipeline. It specifically covered federal easements, Clean Water Act permits and other approvals. Agencies were also told to consider changing a December 2016 memorandum that had paused the Lake Oahe crossing review, withdrawing an environmental-impact-statement notice and relying on earlier environmental assessments. The directive did not itself waive legal requirements or access rights on private property; it directed review, not automatic approval; it repeatedly qualified actions by applicable law and agency judgment. It reversed the prior delay in federal review and advanced a project that had drawn environmental and tribal objections. The memorandum’s wording made the expedited path an executive priority while leaving the formal permitting decisions to the responsible agencies.

description_short: New Yorks attorney general ordered the Trump Foundation to stop soliciting donations for failing to comply with state charity laws.
description_medium: On October 3, 2016, New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman ordered the Trump Foundation to stop soliciting donations in the state. The order required fundraising to cease immediately.
description_long: New York’s attorney general ordered the Donald J. A cease-and-desist letter sent on September 30, 2016, directed the foundation to stop soliciting contributions and told third parties raising money on its behalf to stop as well.
